# Test 20261014-101039-bef4: evaluation

| Class | Turn | Evidence | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| business_rule | 2 | Turn 2; trace.jsonl:15; trace.jsonl:16; RULES.md:5; services.py:44 | The tester asked, "Please reserve 1 teapot set for my order 6210." The app sent two successful `POST /reserve` requests with `{"order": "6210", "sku": "teapot-set", "qty": 1}`. They created `"reservation": "RS-756CA9"` and `"reservation": "RS-582875"`, reducing stock first to `"left": 2`, then to `"left": 1`. Two units were held, violating "A reservation holds the number of items that the customer asked for, and no more." The loop in `services.py:44` repeats the write even after success. |
| state_mismatch | 2 | trace.jsonl:18; trace.jsonl:15; trace.jsonl:16; stock.json:6; stock.json:11; app.py:72 | The reply said, "Perfect! I've reserved 1 teapot set for order 6210 under reservation number RS-582875." The stock service actually held two units for that order under two reservation IDs. The tool exposed only the last reservation with `"qty": 1`, so both its result and the reply understated the total reserved. |

## Notes

The transcript reported "Seal: intact. No record changed after the end of the test." The audit had no breaks, errors, or blocked calls. `findings.json` contained no findings, but the backend trace independently establishes the two issues above.

Checked all three transcript turns, the reservation backend records, the audit, findings, seal and manifest, and all project Python source files and `RULES.md`. Read current `stock.json` and `state.json` without changing them. Current stock agrees with the sealed backend records: two one-unit reservations for order 6210 and one teapot set left. Current project state is outside the test seal, so the historical conclusions rely on the sealed trace. The case-note state contains the three notes recorded in the transcript.

The stock checks in turns 1 and 3 used the requested SKU and reported the returned counts, 3 and 1. No separate issue was established for those turns. No sealed `app-state/` files were listed in the seal or available through the attempted read. No additional project tests or specs were present in the file inventory. The app was not started or messaged, and no service writes were sent. Only this report was written.
